name: Snapp!Trip
label: SNAPP!TRIP
title: Snapp!Trip
lede: Iran’s online travel platform — hotels, flights, trains and buses — inside the Snapp Group. I made its weekly marketing output for three years, and built the brand book it never had.

hero.alt: Snapp!Trip line-art lettering on a red field

meta.label: WHEN
meta.text: Three years in Tehran, from Oct 2020 to Oct 2023.

meta.label: ROLE
meta.text: Graphic designer on the marketing team, turning each campaign brief into the visuals that shipped.

meta.label: TEAM
meta.text: A four-person marketing team: a campaign manager, an art director, a social media specialist, and me on design.

meta.label: SCOPE
meta.text: Campaign key art, social posts, HR branding, illustration and banners, plus the twenty-page visual guideline.

image.alt: The cover of the Snapp!Trip visual design guidelines

feature.label: THE GUIDELINE
feature.title: Twenty pages, so the next person makes the same thing without asking.
feature.text: Logo and clearspace · colour · Iran Sans · three story formats · a pixel, format and weight spec for every banner placement · three icon families

problem.label: THE PROBLEM
problem.title: It inherited a brand from its parent and never had one of its own.
paragraphs: The output ran weekly and never stopped: an email newsletter, Instagram in static and video, Telegram, LinkedIn, website banners, in-app banners in the super app, printed stationery and HR material — with campaign pushes on top of all of it. Four people in marketing touched that output, and one of them was the designer.

Snapp Group fixed the top layer — the logo relationship, the red, the typeface — and below that there was nothing. Illustration, montage style, how a discount figure sat on a banner, what a story looked like: each was decided again per piece, by whoever got there first. So the brand book ran as its own project alongside the marketing calendar, rather than waiting for a quiet month that was never coming.

items.title: Moved the montage from 3D to real photography.
items.text: A 3D montage sells a feeling; a photograph of Istanbul sells a place you can book. The guideline then named three post techniques and three story types, so the choice stopped being taste.
items.cost: every post is now tied to a real photograph of that place existing.

items.title: Split illustration into two families: cities, and theme.
items.text: Cities carry the destination, the theme set carries the campaign. Theme is white line only, low detail, on the dark primary blue — so it still reads at 358×196 beside the booking search.
items.cost: a new city means a new illustration, not a recombination of the old ones.

items.title: Wrote the spec instead of making every asset.
items.text: Eight channels, every week, four people. So every placement was written down: home banner 1073×603 JPEG under 300 KB, title 34 pt, CTA 22 pt; wide banner 1920×320 PNG, no CTA; app banner 1080×705 PNG under 200 KB.
items.cost: a spec has to be maintained; the day it goes stale it starts lying.

outcome.label: OUTCOME
outcome.title: Snapp!Trip ended with an identity of its own.
outcome.text: The illustration families and the montage rule outlived the campaigns they were made for, and the spec meant four people could ship on eight channels a week without deciding the same thing twice.
